title: Fisheries Management
source_note: Standard NUC-aligned Nigerian university 300L Fisheries Management curriculum: principles of fisheries resource management, capture fisheries systems, fishing gears and methods, regulatory and governance tools (licensing, closed seasons, quotas, mesh size regulation), fisheries resources of Nigeria's inland and marine waters, and basic management concepts (MSY, MEY, fishing effort). Overlap with Sustainable Fisheries Management (FIS408) and Fish Stock Assessment (FIS403) is deliberately avoided by keeping this bank on general management tools and governance rather than quantitative stock-assessment models or sustainability/ecosystem theory.

questions.question: Fisheries management is best defined as the:
options: Integrated process of information gathering, analysis, planning, decision-making, and enforcement to sustain fishery resources and achieve stated objectives
Practice of catching as much fish as possible within a fishing season
Study of fish anatomy and physiology for classification purposes
Construction of ponds and hatcheries for fish farming
questions.correct_answer: Integrated process of information gathering, analysis, planning, decision-making, and enforcement to sustain fishery resources and achieve stated objectives
questions.explanation: Fisheries management involves the whole cycle of data collection, regulation-setting, and enforcement aimed at sustaining fish stocks and meeting social, economic, and biological objectives.
questions.topic: Concepts and scope of fisheries management

questions.question: Which of the following is a primary objective of fisheries management?
options: Ensuring the long-term sustainability of fish stocks while optimizing benefits to stakeholders
Maximizing the number of fishing vessels licensed each year
Eliminating all forms of artisanal fishing
Banning aquaculture to protect wild stocks
questions.correct_answer: Ensuring the long-term sustainability of fish stocks while optimizing benefits to stakeholders
questions.explanation: A core objective of fisheries management is balancing sustainable resource use with the economic and social benefits derived by fishers and other stakeholders.
questions.topic: Concepts and scope of fisheries management

questions.question: Capture fisheries, as distinct from aquaculture, refers to:
options: The harvesting of naturally occurring aquatic organisms from the wild
The rearing of fish in controlled ponds and tanks
The breeding of fish under hatchery conditions
The processing of fish after harvest
questions.correct_answer: The harvesting of naturally occurring aquatic organisms from the wild
questions.explanation: Capture fisheries involve catching wild fish stocks from natural water bodies, unlike aquaculture which involves controlled rearing.

questions.question: Which of these is classified as an inland capture fishery resource in Nigeria?
options: Kainji Lake
The Gulf of Guinea continental shelf
The Bight of Benin
Offshore Atlantic waters beyond the EEZ
questions.correct_answer: Kainji Lake
questions.explanation: Kainji Lake is a major inland (freshwater) fishery resource in Nigeria, while the others listed are marine resources.

questions.question: Nigeria's major marine fishing grounds lie mainly along which body of water?
options: The Gulf of Guinea
Lake Chad
The Niger-Benue confluence
The Red Sea
questions.correct_answer: The Gulf of Guinea
questions.explanation: Nigeria's marine capture fisheries operate primarily in the Gulf of Guinea, part of the Atlantic Ocean bordering the country's coastline.

questions.question: A gill net catches fish primarily by:
options: Entangling fish by the gills as they attempt to swim through the mesh
Trapping fish in a funnel-shaped enclosure they cannot exit
Hooking fish on baited lines
Scooping fish from the water surface
questions.correct_answer: Entangling fish by the gills as they attempt to swim through the mesh
questions.explanation: Gill nets are designed so fish swim partway through the mesh and are caught by the gills when they try to back out.

questions.question: Which fishing gear is a passive trap typically used to catch crustaceans and demersal fish by luring them in with bait?
options: Fish trap (basket/pot trap)
Purse seine
Trawl net
Cast net
questions.correct_answer: Fish trap (basket/pot trap)
questions.explanation: Traps such as basket or pot traps are passive gears that lure organisms in with bait and prevent their escape, commonly used for crustaceans and some demersal fish.

questions.question: A purse seine is primarily designed to target:
options: Large schools of pelagic fish near the surface
Individual demersal fish on the sea floor
Fish hiding in rocky crevices
Deep-sea organisms below 1000 metres
questions.correct_answer: Large schools of pelagic fish near the surface
questions.explanation: Purse seines encircle schooling pelagic species like sardines and mackerel near the surface, then are drawn closed at the bottom like a purse.

questions.question: Mesh size regulation is used in fisheries management mainly to:
options: Allow juvenile and undersized fish to escape and reach maturity before capture
Increase the total weight of gear used by fishers
Reduce the cost of manufacturing fishing nets
Make it easier to identify different fishing vessels
questions.correct_answer: Allow juvenile and undersized fish to escape and reach maturity before capture
questions.explanation: Minimum mesh size limits are set so smaller, immature fish can pass through the net and survive to spawn, protecting recruitment to the stock.

questions.question: A closed season in fisheries regulation refers to:
options: A designated period during which fishing for a particular species or in a particular area is prohibited
The period when fish markets are closed for renovation
A season when fish naturally stop reproducing
The period during which hatcheries are not in operation
questions.correct_answer: A designated period during which fishing for a particular species or in a particular area is prohibited
questions.explanation: Closed seasons protect fish, often during spawning periods, by legally restricting fishing activity for a set time.

questions.question: Why are closed seasons commonly timed to coincide with the spawning period of target species?
options: To protect breeding stock and allow successful reproduction before they are exposed to fishing pressure
Because fish are easiest to catch during spawning
Because water levels are lowest during spawning periods
To reduce competition between fishers and fish processors
questions.correct_answer: To protect breeding stock and allow successful reproduction before they are exposed to fishing pressure
questions.explanation: Protecting fish during spawning maximizes reproductive success and recruitment of new individuals into the population.

questions.question: A fishing license or permit system serves fisheries management by:
options: Controlling and monitoring the number and identity of vessels or individuals authorized to fish
Guaranteeing a fixed price for fish at market
Providing free fishing gear to registered fishers
Eliminating the need for closed seasons
questions.correct_answer: Controlling and monitoring the number and identity of vessels or individuals authorized to fish
questions.explanation: Licensing allows authorities to track and limit fishing participants, supporting effort control and enforcement.

questions.question: A total allowable catch (TAC) quota system works by:
options: Setting a maximum total weight or number of fish that may be harvested from a stock in a given period
Fixing the exact number of vessels allowed to dock at a port
Determining the minimum price fishers must sell their catch for
Requiring all fishers to use the same type of gear
questions.correct_answer: Setting a maximum total weight or number of fish that may be harvested from a stock in a given period
questions.explanation: A TAC caps the overall harvest from a stock to prevent overexploitation, and may be subdivided among fishers or fleets.

questions.question: Fishing effort is best described as a measure of:
options: The amount of fishing activity applied to a stock, combining factors such as number of gear units, vessel days, and fishing time
The physical strength required by fishers to haul in nets
The distance travelled by a fishing vessel from port
The total biomass of fish present in a water body
questions.correct_answer: The amount of fishing activity applied to a stock, combining factors such as number of gear units, vessel days, and fishing time
questions.explanation: Fishing effort quantifies the intensity of fishing activity, often expressed as a combination of gear numbers, vessel-days, and time spent fishing.

questions.question: Open-access fisheries are prone to overexploitation mainly because:
options: No individual fisher has exclusive rights to the resource, so there is little incentive to conserve it for future benefit
Fish in open-access waters reproduce more slowly
Open-access waters always have lower fish populations to begin with
Government subsidies are unavailable in open-access systems
questions.correct_answer: No individual fisher has exclusive rights to the resource, so there is little incentive to conserve it for future benefit
questions.explanation: This is the classic 'tragedy of the commons' problem: without ownership or exclusive rights, individuals have little incentive to limit their own catch since restraint benefits everyone, not just them.

questions.question: Co-management in fisheries governance refers to:
options: A shared arrangement where government authorities and local fishing communities jointly participate in managing the resource
Management carried out entirely by private fishing companies
A system where only traditional rulers control fishing rights
Management performed exclusively by international organizations
questions.correct_answer: A shared arrangement where government authorities and local fishing communities jointly participate in managing the resource
questions.explanation: Co-management combines government regulatory authority with the local knowledge and buy-in of resource-user communities to improve compliance and outcomes.

questions.question: Which agency is primarily responsible for federal fisheries regulation and administration in Nigeria?
options: The Federal Department of Fisheries and Aquaculture
The National Emergency Management Agency
The Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation
The Central Bank of Nigeria
questions.correct_answer: The Federal Department of Fisheries and Aquaculture
questions.explanation: The Federal Department of Fisheries and Aquaculture, under the Federal Ministry of Agriculture, oversees national fisheries policy and regulation in Nigeria.

questions.question: Maximum Sustainable Yield (MSY) is defined as:
options: The largest catch that can be taken from a stock indefinitely without depleting it over the long term
The total biomass of all fish species present in a water body
The maximum revenue a fishery can generate in one year
The minimum catch required to keep a fishery economically viable
questions.correct_answer: The largest catch that can be taken from a stock indefinitely without depleting it over the long term
questions.explanation: MSY is the theoretical maximum harvest level a fish population can sustain over time given its natural growth and replacement rate.

questions.question: Overfishing occurs when:
options: Fishing mortality exceeds the rate at which a stock can naturally replace itself through growth and recruitment
Fishers use only legal gear types
The fish population increases faster than fishing pressure
Closed seasons are strictly enforced
questions.correct_answer: Fishing mortality exceeds the rate at which a stock can naturally replace itself through growth and recruitment
questions.explanation: Overfishing happens when the removal rate of fish surpasses the stock's capacity to replenish through reproduction and growth, causing decline.

questions.question: A marine protected area (MPA) contributes to fisheries management primarily by:
options: Providing a refuge where fish stocks can grow and reproduce without fishing pressure, potentially spilling over into adjacent fished areas
Serving as a designated zone for building new fish processing plants
Allowing unrestricted industrial trawling within its boundaries
Replacing the need for mesh size and gear regulations elsewhere
questions.correct_answer: Providing a refuge where fish stocks can grow and reproduce without fishing pressure, potentially spilling over into adjacent fished areas
questions.explanation: MPAs restrict or prohibit fishing to let populations recover, which can enhance stocks in surrounding fished waters through spillover of adults and larvae.

questions.question: Bycatch refers to:
options: Non-target species or undersized individuals caught unintentionally during fishing operations
The main target species a fisher intends to catch
Fish caught specifically for aquaculture broodstock
Fish sold directly at the point of capture
questions.correct_answer: Non-target species or undersized individuals caught unintentionally during fishing operations
questions.explanation: Bycatch is the incidental capture of species, sizes, or sexes not intended to be caught, which is a major concern in fisheries management, especially with non-selective gears like trawls.

questions.question: A cast net is best suited to which fishing scenario?
options: Artisanal fishing in shallow inland waters where a single fisher can throw and retrieve the net by hand
Deep-sea trawling operations beyond the continental shelf
Large-scale industrial purse seining of pelagic schools
Long-line fishing for tuna in open ocean waters
questions.correct_answer: Artisanal fishing in shallow inland waters where a single fisher can throw and retrieve the net by hand
questions.explanation: Cast nets are small, hand-thrown gears typically used by individual artisanal fishers in shallow rivers, lakes, and lagoons.

questions.question: Which factor most directly limits the growth of Nigeria's marine capture fisheries production in recent decades?
options: Declining stock abundance due to overfishing and habitat degradation
A total absence of demand for marine fish products
Excessive rainfall along the coastline
Lack of any fish species in Nigerian coastal waters
questions.correct_answer: Declining stock abundance due to overfishing and habitat degradation
questions.explanation: Nigeria's marine fisheries output has stagnated largely because of overexploitation of key stocks and degradation of coastal habitats such as mangroves.

questions.question: Artisanal fisheries in Nigeria are characterized by:
options: Small-scale, largely traditional operations using canoes and simple gear, contributing the bulk of domestic fish supply
Large industrial trawlers exclusively operating offshore
Fully mechanized deep-sea fleets owned by multinational corporations
Operations restricted only to aquaculture, not capture fisheries
questions.correct_answer: Small-scale, largely traditional operations using canoes and simple gear, contributing the bulk of domestic fish supply
questions.explanation: Artisanal fisheries, using canoes and traditional gear in inland and coastal waters, supply the majority of Nigeria's domestically caught fish.

questions.question: Which management approach directly controls the amount of fishing gear or number of vessels permitted, rather than the total catch?
options: Input (effort) control
Output (catch) control
Technical measures only
Market-based pricing control
questions.correct_answer: Input (effort) control
questions.explanation: Input controls limit fishing capacity itself, such as vessel numbers, gear units, or fishing days, as opposed to output controls, which cap the catch directly.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a technical (gear-based) management measure?
options: Requiring turtle excluder devices on shrimp trawl nets
Setting a national annual catch quota
Licensing individual fishers
Declaring an economic exclusive zone
questions.correct_answer: Requiring turtle excluder devices on shrimp trawl nets
questions.explanation: Technical measures modify gear design or use to reduce unwanted catch or environmental harm, such as turtle excluder devices reducing sea turtle bycatch in shrimp trawls.

questions.question: A long-line fishing gear typically consists of:
options: A main line with numerous baited hooks attached at intervals via branch lines
A single large net dragged behind a vessel
A circular net that encloses a school of fish
A stationary trap baited to attract fish
questions.correct_answer: A main line with numerous baited hooks attached at intervals via branch lines
questions.explanation: Long-lining uses one long main line fitted with many baited hooks on branch lines (snoods), targeting species such as tuna and sharks.

questions.question: The concept of 'fishing rights' or 'tenure' in fisheries management is important because it:
options: Gives individuals or communities a stake in the resource, encouraging more sustainable use
Guarantees that all fishers receive equal income regardless of effort
Removes the need for any government regulation
Only applies to aquaculture, not capture fisheries
questions.correct_answer: Gives individuals or communities a stake in the resource, encouraging more sustainable use
questions.explanation: Secure tenure or use rights create incentives for stewardship, since those with rights benefit directly from conserving the resource for future use.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a 'trawl net'?
options: A large, cone-shaped net towed through the water or along the seabed to catch fish or shrimp
A small hand-thrown circular net used in shallow water
A stationary basket trap for catching crustaceans
A line fitted with a single hook and bait
questions.correct_answer: A large, cone-shaped net towed through the water or along the seabed to catch fish or shrimp
questions.explanation: Trawls are actively towed, cone-shaped nets used for demersal (bottom) or midwater fishing, common in industrial fisheries.

questions.question: Why is stakeholder participation (fishers, processors, traders, communities) considered important in fisheries management planning?
options: It improves compliance and the practicality of regulations by incorporating local knowledge and building ownership of the rules
It eliminates the need for scientific data collection
It guarantees higher fish prices at market
It allows the government to withdraw entirely from fisheries oversight
questions.correct_answer: It improves compliance and the practicality of regulations by incorporating local knowledge and building ownership of the rules
questions.explanation: Involving stakeholders in decision-making tends to produce more realistic, better-accepted regulations and higher voluntary compliance.

questions.question: Monitoring, Control, and Surveillance (MCS) in fisheries management primarily supports:
options: Enforcement of regulations by tracking fishing activity and detecting illegal, unreported, or unregulated (IUU) fishing
The construction of new fishing harbours
The formulation of fish pricing policy
The breeding of improved fish varieties
questions.correct_answer: Enforcement of regulations by tracking fishing activity and detecting illegal, unreported, or unregulated (IUU) fishing
questions.explanation: MCS systems (patrols, vessel monitoring systems, catch reporting) are the enforcement arm of fisheries management, used to detect and deter IUU fishing.

questions.question: A minimum legal size limit for a harvested species is a management tool intended to:
options: Protect juvenile fish so they can reach reproductive maturity before being caught
Standardize the size of fishing vessels
Set the price paid to fishers per kilogram of fish
Determine which fishing gear is legal to use
questions.correct_answer: Protect juvenile fish so they can reach reproductive maturity before being caught
questions.explanation: Minimum size limits ensure fish have the chance to spawn at least once before being legally harvested, supporting stock recruitment.

questions.question: Which scenario best illustrates a conflict typically managed within fisheries governance?
options: Artisanal fishers and industrial trawlers competing for the same inshore fishing grounds
Two fish farmers disagreeing over feed brand preference
A processor choosing between smoking and freezing fish
A researcher selecting a statistical method for a survey
questions.correct_answer: Artisanal fishers and industrial trawlers competing for the same inshore fishing grounds
questions.explanation: User conflicts, such as between small-scale and industrial fishers over the same grounds, are a classic governance challenge addressed through zoning and regulation.
